prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1182; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representative, who advised that the policyholder's vehicle was sideswiped while changing lanes and that the policyholder sustained a wrist fracture. The claim was opened and assigned for investigation.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the vehicle was covered at the time of loss. Requested the police report and photographs from the scene.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photographs, which confirm some details of the reported impact. No independent witnesses have come forward, and the only accounts so far come from the parties involved.

Entry 4: Police records and statements from responding parties confirm the claimant was present in the vehicle at the scene. Vehicle damage appears consistent with the sideswipe described, with the damaged panels lining up with the other vehicle's contact points.

Entry 5: Obtained the medical records for the claimant's wrist fracture. The injury is the type and severity expected from a force of this kind, and the treatment followed a usual course.

Entry 6: Medical file shows the claimant's treatment tapered off steadily as recovery progressed. No prior injury to the same wrist or arm appears in the records reviewed so far.

Entry 7: Spoke again with the claimant's representative, who confirmed the claimant's account of the lane change. The claimant has described the events the same way in every conversation to date.

Entry 8: Our records show no earlier damage to the insured vehicle. A neighbor contacted us and believes the car was already damaged a few weeks before the claimed date. This statement has not yet been verified and is being noted for follow-up.

Entry 9: Requested the repair estimate and photographs of the vehicle from the repair facility to compare against the impact described and the earlier damage concern raised by the neighbor.

Entry 10: Reviewed the neighbor's account alongside the vehicle records and photographs. The question of pre-existing damage remains open pending further inquiry into the timing.

Entry 11: File remains open. Next steps are to obtain a recorded statement from the neighbor and confirm the repair history before any settlement decision is made.
